## Invariant checks: zero in, zero out, and the global budgets {#sec-ch15-invariants}

### Summary

The sections before this one read assertions that a test already makes. This one asks a different question:
which properties of the solver would survive every test in the catalogue and still be wrong? Two answers recur in
this project's own defect record.[^ch15-inv-motive] The first is a species that is not there: a floor meant to keep
a divide finite instead reports an absent amount as present, the update consumes it, and the row goes negative.
The second is a global total that no test watches: mass, energy or angular momentum drifts slowly, and because no
single step is wrong by much, nothing fails.

Both are invariant defects. The checks here are built to fail on exactly those: one asks that an absent species
have a zero rate and no negative amount after many implicit steps, and lists every positivity floor, clamp and
epsilon in the covered paths with a measurement of what that floor changes; the other accumulates global mass,
total energy and, for the cubed sphere, global axial angular momentum over many steps and reports the drift per
step and where it comes from. Every claim carries a break arm that removes one term and makes it red. A check
that cannot be made to fail is not finished, so the green run executes every break arm and requires it to fail.
Two claims carry no arm and the chapter does not pretend otherwise: `[Z5]` is an inventory, and an inventory
cannot be broken from inside the check that owns the list; and `[Z6]`/`[B6]` are the arm-runners themselves.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** States the invariants a catalogue of per-test assertions does not cover: zero in, zero out, and the three global budgets.

**Data.** Ported operators on a six-panel gnomonic-equiangular shell; a measured run of a build at the pin for the drift of a flowing state.

**Placement.** Analysis of the update operator, outside the solver step; the run record is a full six-panel integration.

**Activation.** None for the checks; the run record needs a build at the pin and, for its GPU[^rg-3464cea88887] arm, a CUDA-enabled one.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact identities and measured drifts for the configurations tested; a budget that closes here is not a claim about any other deck.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch15-inv-claims and @tbl-ch15-inv-run.
:::

Local symbols: $\theta_{15}$ the dimensionless positivity scale factor of the flux limiter [-]; $L_z$ the global
axial angular momentum [$\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$]; $\Omega_c$ the solid angle of one cubed-sphere cell [sr];
$\lambda$ the latitude [rad]. The rest is appendix A: $V_i$, $A_{i\pm1/2}$, $\rho$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$, $x_1,
x_2, x_3$ and the cell indices $i, j, k$.

### Derivation

Four identities carry the claims below. Each is tied to the statement in the code that makes it true, and each
has a term whose removal makes it false.

#### Zero in, zero out

Let $u \geq 0$ be one species row and let $A_{j\pm1/2}F_{j\pm1/2}$ be the area-weighted face fluxes the
divergence uses. The flux limiter
({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}}) accumulates the *outgoing* part of those
fluxes only, through a rectifier on the upper face and on the negated lower face, and compares it with what the
cell has:

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_i&=\Delta t\sum_{\text{faces}}\max(\pm A F, 0),\\
\theta_{15,i}&=\begin{cases}
\min\!\left(1,\;\dfrac{\max(u_i,0)\,V_i\,(1-4096\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m})}{D_i}\right), & D_i>0,\\[2ex]
1, & D_i=0 .
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch15-inv-theta}

The numerator is the cell's own amount put through a rectifier, not through a floor. For an absent row
$u_i = 0$ the numerator is exactly zero, so $\theta_{15,i}=0$, and the scaling pass
({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_scale_ >}}) multiplies every donor face of that cell by
it. The row cannot be drained at all, and stays bitwise zero for any number of steps. Replace the rectifier by a
floor at $10^{-300}$ and the numerator is positive: the cell is treated as holding that amount, the update
removes it, and the row goes negative — which is the defect this check exists to catch.

That guarantee is only ever *exercised* where the absent row is actually drained. $\theta_{15}$ is
$\min(1,\,\text{avail}/\text{drain})$ on the cells with $\text{drain}>0$ and exactly $1$ everywhere else
({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}}, the `torch::where` on `drain > 0.`), and the
numerator — the only place the rectifier appears — is not consulted on the `else` branch. An identically zero
row reconstructs to zero on both sides of every face, which is claim `[Z4]` below, so its species flux, and
hence its drain, is identically zero: the rectifier is never reached for such a row. Instrumenting
`flux_positivity_theta` at the pin and running the compiled record of @tbl-ch15-inv-run measures exactly that —
over the 162 limiter calls of three cycles on six panels, the two absent channels have
$\max(\text{drain}) = 0$ and no cell at all with $\text{drain}>0$, against a maximum drain of
$2.274\times10^{13}$ over 2456 cells for the present control channel.

So the two pieces of evidence below are credited with different things, and this is the sharpest statement each
supports. `[Z1]` tests the rectifier, because it prescribes the face fluxes of the absent row directly and can
therefore put it in the draining state the solver will not produce on its own; replacing the rectifier by the
floor turns `[Z1]` red. The compiled record tests something weaker but end-to-end: that an absent row survives
the implicit solve, the moist limiter and the cross-panel exchange still bitwise zero. It does **not** test the
rectifier, and we should not claim it does — with the rectifier replaced by a $10^{-300}$ floor in the built
library the record stays green on both CPU and CUDA, exactly because the drain it would act on is zero. The
honest reading is that two independent mechanisms protect an absent row, a zero flux and a zero factor, and that
the record exercises the first while `[Z1]` exercises the second.

Two further absent-species paths close the same way. The condensate repair
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}) borrows a deficit
$\min(c,0)$ from the parent vapour and then writes $\max(c,0)$; both are exactly zero for $c=0$, so an absent
condensate borrows nothing. The reconstruction's face clamp
({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp >}}) has nothing to repair, because a limited slope over an identically zero
stencil is zero before any clamp.

#### A floor is only honest if you can say what it changes

A floor is not a property of the scheme; it is a repair, and a repair that nobody measures is indistinguishable
from a bug. The inventory in the Tests layer therefore sorts every floor, clamp and epsilon in the covered paths
into six kinds and measures each: a **state** floor changes a stored value and is reported as the mass, energy or
pressure it invents; a **guard** sits under a division and is shown to bind only at or below its own value; a
**select** keeps a sign or a cap; a **domain** clamp holds an argument inside the domain of the next function; an
**index** clamp changes which cell is read and never a value; an **eps** decides a branch or leaves a stated
fraction behind; and a **cap** is a deck choice that changes the answer whenever it binds. The one guard that
shares its value with the defect that motivated this section, the $10^{-300}$ under the drain division, is shown
to change no *selected* value at all: the surrounding `where` picks the quotient only where the denominator is
positive, so the guard exists to stop the discarded branch evaluating $1/0$.

#### The volume-weighted budget and its measure

@eq-ch15-budget already gives the telescoping identity: the volume-weighted total is constant when both
neighbours of every face use the same flux. Two things can break it without any test noticing. The first is a
seam where two blocks do not share a face flux; the second is a volume measure that is not the exact integral of
the same solid angle the $x_1$ face area uses. On the cubed sphere the cell volume is
({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::cell_volume >}})

$$
V_{kji}=\frac{r_{i+1/2}^3-r_{i-1/2}^3}{3}\,\Omega_{c,kj},
\qquad
A_{1,kji\pm1/2}=r_{i\pm1/2}^2\,\Omega_{c,kj},
$$ {#eq-ch15-inv-volume}

with $\Omega_{c,kj}$ the exact solid angle of the gnomonic cell, a corner sum of
$\arctan\!\big(xy/\sqrt{1+x^2+y^2}\big)$ over the four corners
({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::face_area1 >}}). Because the same $\Omega_c$
appears in both, the discrete divergence of the radial field $r\hat{\mathbf r}$ is exactly $3$, and the six
panels' volumes sum to the shell's. The trapezoid $\tfrac12(A_{i-1/2}+A_{i+1/2})\,\Delta r$ passes neither, by
$O((\Delta r/r)^2)$.

#### Why the uniform-pressure state exerts no tangential force

The axial angular momentum of a closed, unforced shell is exactly conserved, so any drift is numerical. The first
place to look is the resting state. On the cubed sphere an $x_2$ face carries, in the local orthonormal frame,
only the normal pressure; the covariance transform
({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::flux2global2_ >}}) leaves the covariant rows
$p\sin\vartheta_{j\pm1/2}$ and $0$. The geometric source of the same row
({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::forward >}}) is $p$[^rg-e1cf79cb49cd] times the cached quantity
built in ({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::reset >}}),

$$
\left(\frac{x}{rD}\right)_{kji}
=\frac{\big(A_{2}\sin\vartheta\big)_{k,j+1/2,i}-\big(A_{2}\sin\vartheta\big)_{k,j-1/2,i}}{V_{kji}} .
$$ {#eq-ch15-inv-metric}

The numerator is the difference of the *same product* that the pressure flux divergence forms, so for a uniform
$p$ the two cancel exactly: only the order of two multiplications differs between them. The cancellation is not
a truncation statement but an identity, and it is what keeps a resting atmosphere from spinning itself up.
Replace @eq-ch15-inv-metric by the analytic metric derivative — the same term to truncation order, a different
number — and the resting state acquires a tangential force of order the term itself.

The axial projection needs the Cartesian velocity, which the panel transform
({{< code src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.cpp cs_contra_to_cart_ >}}) supplies from the contravariant components
after the covariant momentum is raised; then

$$
L_z=\sum_{kji}\rho_{kji}\,\big(\mathbf r\times\mathbf v\big)_{z,kji}\,V_{kji}
=\sum_{kji}\rho_{kji}\,u_{\text{east},kji}\,r_i\cos\lambda_{kj}\,V_{kji}.
$$ {#eq-ch15-inv-lz}

### Numerical method

The two checks are ports: they execute no compiled snapy, so they run from a fresh clone with numpy alone, and
`src/tests` discovers them like any other check in this report. A port is only worth its numbers if it is the
same arithmetic, so every geometric quantity and the velocity transform were compared cell by cell against a
build at the pin, on all six panels, at four resolutions up to 45 cells per panel edge. At the coarsest
resolution 14 of the 16 compared quantities agree **bit for bit**; the rest agree within the conditioning of the
formula, which is derived in the Limits layer and is not a port error.

The run record is the complement: a six-panel integration of the real solver on a shell, with a discretely
balanced isothermal rest state and a solid-body zonal wind, closed radial walls, no drag, no sponge and no
topography. Its system has no external torque, so the exact drift of all three budgets is zero and every measured
slope is numerical. It runs on CPU and, with a CUDA-enabled build, on the GPU.

| run | mass | energy and potential | $L_z$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPU, 8 cells per panel edge, 400 cycles | $-6.0\times10^{-17}$ | $-1.0\times10^{-10}$ | $+6.0\times10^{-8}$ |
| CPU, 16, 400 cycles | $-6.0\times10^{-17}$ | $+1.8\times10^{-11}$ | $-5.0\times10^{-10}$ |
| CPU, 24, 400 cycles | $-5.6\times10^{-17}$ | $-1.6\times10^{-11}$ | $-5.9\times10^{-10}$ |
| CPU, 16, 2000 cycles | $-5.9\times10^{-17}$ | $-2.4\times10^{-12}$ | $-9.9\times10^{-10}$ |
| CPU, 8, 400 cycles, at rest | $-6.0\times10^{-17}$ | $-4.8\times10^{-17}$ | $L_z \equiv 0$ |
| CUDA, 8, 400 cycles | $-6.0\times10^{-17}$ | $-1.0\times10^{-10}$ | $+6.0\times10^{-8}$ |
| CUDA, 16, 400 cycles | $-5.9\times10^{-17}$ | $+1.8\times10^{-11}$ | $-5.0\times10^{-10}$ |
| CUDA, 8, 400 cycles, at rest | $-6.0\times10^{-17}$ | $-4.8\times10^{-17}$ | $L_z \equiv 0$ |

: Measured relative drift per cycle of the three global budgets, six panels on a shell at the code pin. {#tbl-ch15-inv-run}

Read @tbl-ch15-inv-run as follows.[^ch15-inv-run] Mass is at round-off at every resolution and on both devices:
the volume-weighted total of @eq-ch15-budget holds in the solver, not only in the port. Energy, with the
potential carried, is also at round-off in the resting state, $-4.8\times10^{-17}$ per cycle, which says that the
gravity work booked at the faces closes the budget exactly; with the flow it is four to six orders larger, and
that part is the scheme's own dissipation, not a bookkeeping error. $L_z$ is the one budget that is neither: it
is $10^{-8}$ to $10^{-10}$ of itself per cycle, far above mass and above the resting energy drift, it changes
sign and falls steeply between the coarsest grid and the next, and in the resting state it stays identically
zero. So the drift is a property of the flowing solution, not of the geometry, and it is not at round-off.

CPU and CUDA agree to all four printed digits of the energy and $L_z$ drift of the two flowing runs, and differ
in the last digit of the mass round-off; in the resting run, where the energy drift is itself at round-off, the
two differ in its third digit ($-4.829\times10^{-17}$ against $-4.837\times10^{-17}$). No row is a device-only
result: every row of @tbl-ch15-inv-run exists on CPU, and the three CUDA rows repeat CPU rows on the GPU.

`[Z1]` is a statement about the limiter alone, so it has a run record of its own: the same shell, with the
four-species moist thermodynamics and the NH$_3$ + H$_2$S nucleation of `tests/test_condensate_conservation.yaml`,
the conserved limiter switched **on**, an implicit $x_1$ solve, and a warm bubble to make the implicit solve and
the species transport do real work. NH$_3$ is present and is the control; H$_2$S and its condensate NH$_4$SH are
set to exactly zero. Six green arms were run.[^ch15-inv-absent] In all six — 2000 cycles at 8 cells per panel
edge, 200 at 16, implicit schemes 9 and 1 and the explicit scheme 0, on CPU and on the GPU — **both absent rows hold zero non-zero
entries in every interior cell of all six panels at every cycle**, and their global masses stay at exactly
$0$. The present row is never driven negative either: its smallest value over 2000 cycles is
$+2.97\times10^{-6}$, against an initial $10^{-3}$. The CPU and GPU arms agree to every printed digit, including
the final species masses $5.831574\times10^{15}$ and $5.186102\times10^{15}$ kg.

A species repaired *inside* a stage is back at or above zero by the time the cycle ends, so reading the state at
the cycle boundary cannot see it; the only trace is the line the thermodynamics prints when it repairs one. The
script therefore captures file descriptor 1 across the whole run and counts those lines. **Every green arm
reports zero of them.** That is the stronger statement: not merely that the absent rows are zero when each cycle
ends, but that nothing was repaired at any stage of any cycle.

The break arm makes the counter fire. `blob-no-limiter` gives the two rows a discontinuous top-hat of
$10^{-6}$ and switches the conserved limiter off; the reconstruction then undershoots across the edge of the hat
and, on CPU, the run reports `Warning: Negative concentration for species 2 = -8.7005e-321. Setting it to zero.`
twice, and the script exits 1. `blob-limiter` is the same top-hat with the limiter back on: zero repair lines.
The pair is what identifies the responsible term — the limiter, not the smoothness of the field. This is the
same pathology `tests/test_flux_positivity.py` describes at the pin, "the very repair-instead-of-prevention
pathology the limiter removes" ({{< code tests/test_flux_positivity.py >}}), reproduced on the six-panel shell.

Two results of that run are negative findings and are reported as such. First, `--break floor-seed`, which starts
the two rows at the $10^{-300}$ a concentration floor would leave behind, **does not go red**: over 200 implicit
cycles the seeded rows stay at or above zero and nothing is repaired. The kintera defect needed an implicit
kinetics source to consume the floored amount; this deck runs transport, the limiter and the equation of state
and no kinetics, and that is not enough on its own. Second, `blob-no-limiter` is red on CPU and **not** on the
GPU, where the same arm reports zero repair lines. Whether the GPU arm does not undershoot or the repair is
reported only from the host path is a hypothesis this report has not tested.

The port was validated against the build at the pin.[^ch15-inv-port] Sixteen quantities, on six panels, at four
resolutions: all sixteen agree within the conditioning bound at every resolution, and fourteen agree bit for bit
at the coarsest.

: Where the invariants live in the code. {#tbl-ch15-inv-code}

**How to run the checks.** They import numpy and nothing else. From the report directory (@sec-appa-refresh):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 src/snapy_report/ch15/checks/invariants_zero_check.py
PYTHONPATH=src python3 src/snapy_report/ch15/checks/invariants_budget_check.py
```

Each prints one `[Cn] PASS` line per claim, exits 0, and ends with the count of claims that passed. The last
claim of each runs every break arm and requires it to fail, so a green run is also the evidence that the arms go
red.

**How to run one break arm on its own.** `--list-breaks` names them; `--break <arm>` runs that one and is
**expected to exit nonzero**:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 src/snapy_report/ch15/checks/invariants_zero_check.py --list-breaks
PYTHONPATH=src python3 src/snapy_report/ch15/checks/invariants_budget_check.py --break B1-seam
```

**How to reproduce the run record.** It needs a build at the pin installed in the active Python, and a
CUDA-enabled one for `--device cuda`:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python3 src/snapy_report/ch15/evidence/aam_budget_run.py \
    --device cpu --nx 16 --cycles 2000 --omega 2.0e-5
PYTHONPATH=src python3 src/snapy_report/ch15/evidence/absent_species_run.py \
    --device cpu --nx 8 --cycles 2000 --scheme 9
PYTHONPATH=src python3 src/snapy_report/ch15/evidence/port_validation.py --nx 45 --nr 8
```

`absent_species_run.py` is the one run record that asserts: it exits nonzero if either absent row acquires a
non-zero entry at any cycle. The other two report and exit 0.

A CUDA-enabled build needs one extra step, which `aam_budget_run.py` performs for its `cuda` arm: the extension
passes the CUDA sidecar to the linker but references no symbol in it, because its kernels register themselves
through static initialisers, so the linker drops it under `--as-needed` and a device tensor reaches an empty
dispatcher. The sidecar is loaded explicitly, after torch and with global visibility, before the first device
tensor exists.

**The rectifier in the code.** The numerator of @eq-ch15-inv-theta in
({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp flux_positivity_theta >}}) is

```cpp
double margin = kPositivityRoundoffUlp * machine_epsilon(u.scalar_type());
auto avail = u.relu() * pcoord->cell_volume() * (1. - margin);
```

`relu`, not `clamp_min` with a small positive value: that one choice is what makes an absent row's factor exactly
zero rather than a tiny positive number.

: The invariant claims and the arm that breaks each. {#tbl-ch15-inv-claims}

Both checks were run for this chapter and their output is the committed
`invariants_zero_check.out` and `invariants_budget_check.out`.[^ch15-inv-checks-run] The green numbers:

- **[Z1]** the absent row's first-step tendency is $0$ in all 48 cells and the row holds 0 non-zero entries after
  2000 steps, minimum $+0$. Under `Z1-floor` the same row's tendency is $6.2\times10^{-299}$, it holds 96000
  non-zero entries and its minimum is $-2.0\times10^{-297}$. The same claim holds in the compiled solver, with
  the implicit $x_1$ solve and the moist limiter on: see the run record above.[^ch15-inv-absent]
- **[Z5]** 65 sites in 29 groups: 15 state, 19 guard, 5 select, 6 domain, 6 index, 5 eps, 2 cap, 7 meter. The
  state group invents, on 4000 probe cells, $5.1\times10^{-4}$ of dry mass at the density floor and
  $3.9\times10^{1}$ of total energy at the energy floor; the $10^{-300}$ drain guard changes none of the
  *selected* quotients.
- **[B1]** relative mass drift $+1.6\times10^{-19}$ per step and $-1.3\times10^{-16}$ over 2000 steps, against
  the reduction bound $5.7\times10^{-14}$. Under `B1-seam`, with the two sides of one interior face differing by
  one part in a thousand, it is $-4.1\times10^{-14}$ per step and $-8.1\times10^{-11}$ over the run.
- **[B2]** relative energy drift $-5.2\times10^{-19}$ per step and $-1.6\times10^{-16}$ over the run; under
  `B2-cellwork` $+2.9\times10^{-15}$ per step and $+5.8\times10^{-12}$ over the run.
- **[B3]** the six panels' solid angles sum to $-1.1\times10^{-16}$ of $4\pi$, their volumes to $0$ of the
  shell's, and $\max|\nabla\cdot(r\hat{\mathbf r})-3| = 3.2\times10^{-14}$ over 6912 cells; under
  `B3-trapezoid` the volumes miss by $1.1\times10^{-5}$ and the divergence by $3.4\times10^{-5}$.
- **[B4]** the largest covariant tangential force density on the resting shell is $2.5\times10^{-17}$ against a
  single term of $1.35\times10^{-2}$, i.e. $1.8\times10^{-15}$ relative; under `B4-analytic` the same quantity is
  $1.0\times10^{-1}$, which is $7.6$ times the term itself.

  `B4-analytic` is a **wrong-formula arm, not a truncation-order variant**: it is not "the same term to
  truncation order" that the name might suggest. Measured against the discrete source at $p_0=10^5$, the
  largest $|\mathrm{src}_2|$ is

  ```
  n_ang      discrete       analytic    analytic/discrete
      8    1.3499e-02    1.1622e-01      8.61
     16    1.4994e-02    2.3622e-01     15.75
     32    1.5773e-02    4.7525e-01     30.13
     45    1.6004e-02    6.6946e-01     41.83
  ```

  The discrete source converges with refinement while the analytic branch grows roughly like
  $n_\mathrm{ang}$, i.e. like the inverse cell width, so the two never approach each other: the gap widens from
  $7.6$ to $40.8$ times the discrete term between 8 and 45 cells per panel edge. The ratio tracks
  $n_\mathrm{ang}$ closely enough to suggest a single missing angular factor, but restoring a $d\beta$ and the
  $C/D$ ratio only stops the growth and leaves a constant factor near $2.9$, so the arm is not one factor away
  from being a truncation-order variant; we leave it as the wrong-formula arm it is rather than ship a
  substitute we cannot derive. It remains a valid break arm -- it shows the claim is sensitive to this source
  term -- but it does not demonstrate the delicacy a truncation-order perturbation would.
- **[B5]** $L_z$ drifts $+5.5\times10^{-8}\ \mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$ per step, which is $8.7\times10^{-34}$ of
  what the same cells carry at one metre per second eastward; under `B5-odd-panel`, with one of the six panels
  assembled from the analytic metric and the other five from the discrete one, the drift is
  $-6.9\times10^{24}$ per step, or $11\%$ of that reference every step.

  This claim's bound is $10^{-20}$ per step. A bound of $10^{-15}$ cannot see this claim's own term being
  deleted: removing the geometric pressure source outright on **all six** panels leaves the drift at
  $-2.1\times10^{-18}$ per step, and replacing it by the analytic derivative on all six leaves it at
  $-1.5\times10^{-17}$, and both clear $10^{-15}$. The odd-panel arm catches only the *inconsistency* between
  panels, never the term itself. The arm `B5-nosource` deletes the source on all six panels and is red against
  the bound set here, which the shipped operator clears with fourteen orders of margin
  ($8.7\times10^{-34}$ against $10^{-20}$).

### What each claim does and does not test

An independent review asked a sharper question than "does the arm go red": does the claim still pass when the
term it credits is **deleted**? That is not what most of the arms above do -- they inject a defect (a positive
floor, an odd panel) rather than removing a guard. Running each term-removal explicitly, on the committed
checks at this pin:

- `[Z1]`, the rectifier `u.relu()`: **goes red** -- but on the *present* control row, which reaches
  $-9.9\times10^{-324}$, two subnormal units, not on the absent row.
- `[Z2]`, both reconstruction clamps, or the rectifier: still passes. For $u=0$ exactly, `relu(u)` and `u` are
  the same number.
- `[Z3]`, the $\max(c,0)$ clamp, or the $\min(c,0)$ borrow gate: still passes.
- `[Z4]`, the reconstruction face clamp, on a genuinely zero row: still passes.
- `[B2]`, the potential-flux face term: still passes.
- `[B5]`, the geometric pressure source on all six panels: passes against a $10^{-15}$ bound; **fails** against
  the $10^{-20}$ bound this chapter sets.

The pattern in the zero-in/zero-out family is one fact, not five: **every one of these guards is a no-op on an
exactly zero row.** A limited slope over a zero stencil is zero before any clamp; $\min(0,0)$ and $\max(0,0)$
are zero; `relu(0)` is `0`. So the right reading of `[Z2]`--`[Z4]` is that *nothing in the absent-species path
manufactures a non-zero from zero*, which is a real and checkable property, and not that any particular clamp
is what holds the row at zero. The guards earn their place on rows that have gone slightly negative, which is a
different claim, and `Z4-noclamp` -- which seeds one cell at $-10^{-18}$ -- is in fact a test of that different
claim rather than of `[Z4]` as stated. The arms that remain are defect-injection arms, and they are the right
ones for this family: the failure mode worth guarding against is the positive concentration floor of the
kintera defect this section opens with, not a missing clamp. `[Z2]` carries `Z2-floor` on the same principle.

`[B2]` is narrowed rather than re-armed. The diagnostic is $\sum (E + \rho\phi)V$, and dropping the
potential-flux face term leaves $\phi_\mathrm{cell}\,\nabla\!\cdot\!(A F_m)$ cancelling against the
potential term identically, so the global total is conserved whatever that face term does. No tolerance can
recover sensitivity here; the check genuinely tests only that the cell-velocity booking fails where the face
booking holds. Showing that the face term is right locally needs a different diagnostic, which this chapter
does not have.

`[B5]` is the one case where tightening the claim is enough, and it matters: against $10^{-15}$ the claim
passes with its own source deleted on all six panels.

### Limits

**The checks do not integrate a flowing solution.** `[B4]` and `[B5]` establish an identity of the resting state
and accumulate its round-off; they say nothing about a state with a circulation, because the port carries no
Riemann solver and no cross-panel exchange. The measured drift of a flowing state is in the run record, and only
there.

**Each run record is one deck.** The budget record is six panels in one process on a thin shell, dry ideal gas,
closed radial walls, constant radial gravity, solid-body rotation and no forcing. A budget that closes on it is
not a claim about a deck with sedimentation, sponges or more than one block per panel. The angular-momentum drift
it measures is the drift of *this* configuration; it is reported, not explained. The absent-species record adds
the moist thermodynamics, the conserved limiter and an implicit $x_1$ solve to the same shell, but it is still
one block per panel in one process, and it runs no kinetics between steps: the reaction is declared so that the
species rows exist, and the driver-level kinetics of @sec-ch10-kinetics is not called. An absent species crossing
a *rank* seam, and an absent species through a kinetics source, are outside both records.

**The angular metric is ill-conditioned at high resolution.** The angular cell widths are an arccosine of a
quantity that approaches one as the grid refines: $1-u \approx (d/2)^2$ for an angular width $d$, so arccosine
amplifies a last-bit difference in $u$ by $1/\sqrt{1-u^2}$, and the relative error of the width itself grows as
$\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/d^2$. Two conforming implementations of the same formula therefore differ by that much, and
the cached difference of two such widths by about four times more: $3.7\times10^{-13}$ at 8 cells per panel edge
and $1.2\times10^{-11}$ at 45. That is a bound on how precisely any statement about the metric can be made at
those resolutions, and it is six orders below the angular-momentum drift measured above, so it does not account
for it.

**An inventory is a snapshot of one pin.** The 65 sites of `[Z5]` are the floors, clamps and epsilons of the
paths this chapter covers at the code pin, not of every path in the repository; a floor added elsewhere is
outside it until the inventory is rerun. The pin predates the work on the angular-momentum
drift,[^ch15-inv-pinlag] so nothing here measures any fix for it: the numbers describe the code at the pin and
must be read again when the pin moves.

**Round-off at subnormal magnitudes.** The 4096-epsilon margin of @eq-ch15-inv-theta is a *relative* margin, so
it underflows once a cell is drained into the subnormal range. `[Z1]`'s present control row reaches
$-4.9\times10^{-324}$, one subnormal unit below zero, after 2000 steps. The absent row never does, because its
factor is exactly zero rather than merely small — which is the distinction the whole section is about.
